title: Cross-Border Payments Operations
thesis: Snowflake turns daily route activity from a synthetic Singapore payments hub into straight-through and exception KPIs, 7-day payment-failure risk scores, screening anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Straight-through rate, exceptions raised, failed payments and SGD value processed for 40 routes from Singapore into Malaysia, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Thailand and the Philippines.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to route-day rows.
The exception-type chart shows which exceptions end as failed payments and which always clear, such as clearing system outages.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of payments KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which routes should the exceptions team watch first?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each route's probability of a failed payment in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent 14 days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags screening hit rate outliers per route, and the forecast projects hub-wide exception volume for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

talking_points: Nostro reconciliation compliance, correspondent due-diligence coverage and pending documents frame the control gaps.
Reconciliation compliance against failed payments by route shows where weak reconciliation and failures move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, route, exception-type and risk tables only.
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a payment drops into exception right now?

talking_points: Live payment events land in RAW.LIVE_PAYMENTS, from the simulator or from Amazon Data Firehose through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs EXCEPTION events with an SOP hint and the route's current risk band, then emails the on-call analyst.
tabs.call_out: From payment exception to case in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over 14 synthetic exception-handling SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (Data Firehose, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
